assessment: The incumbent achieved intended course sets in 32/40 exports and a 17-minute handling median, missing both targets. A concrete limiting observation is the seven-minute median for 24 exports with unchanged assignments: scheduled CSV production already supports low effort in that subgroup. Six affected exports coincided with assignment changes and two with renames, suggesting investigation without establishing causation. No sampled cross-center rows supports only that sample; the course-split center was absent. Short runtime and slow replacement delivery do not reveal active handling costs.

openings.claim: Current instructor assignments or mutable course names may cause exporter and coordinator disagreement about the requested week’s course set.
openings.delta: Locate disagreement in export selection versus the intended-course reference before changing selection logic.
openings.prediction: If selection causes the problem, changing current assignments or names while holding the agreed historical course set constant will change inclusion. If references cause it, exports may remain consistent while coordinator expectations differ.
openings.probe: In fabricated staging fixtures, vary assignment timing and renames independently. Agree intended courses with consenting coordinators, then compare selections using stable identifiers where available. Include a course split and verify every exported row’s center ownership.
assumptions: Historical assignment data and stable identifiers may be unavailable.
Keep participants private, CSV schema unchanged and attendance entry available.
Bound diagnosis within six engineer-days and existing hosting.

openings.claim: Does replacement coordination consume active handling time, or mainly add elapsed waiting?
openings.delta: Distinguish the handling target from replacement latency; runtime cannot identify the dominant handling cost.
openings.prediction: If requests and follow-up dominate affected cases, active minutes will cluster there. If checking or importing dominates, shortening delivery alone will leave most handling work intact.
openings.probe: Use two short sessions per consenting coordinator to observe fabricated first-use and replacement workflows. Time checking, correction requests, follow-up, downloading and importing separately; record inactive waiting separately. Prioritize one bounded change for evaluation across the next 40 exports.
assumptions: Fabricated workflows support prioritization, not proof of production targets.
Use authorized workspaces, documented CSV and existing resources; attendance entry continues.
Share the six engineer-day budget with the first probe.
